headline: Docker has published a standard way to package an AI agent with a reviewable list of what it may access, and is taking the standard to the CNCF, an open-source foundation.
score_reason: Lowered from 5: the announcement was on 24 Sep 2026, over a week old, CNCF acceptance is not confirmed, and only Docker's own product supports it so far.
importance_line: Teams that let AI agents work with their code or accounts could review what each agent may touch in one standard file, but the standard is new, only Docker's own product runs it so far, and the CNCF has not been reported as accepting it.
summary: InfoQ reports that Docker announced on 24 Sep 2026 that it is bringing its Sandbox Kit Specification, now at version 3, to the Cloud Native Computing Foundation (CNCF); it packs an AI agent, its tools and a typed list of the websites, passwords and folders it asks for into an ordinary container image so the permissions can be reviewed. InfoQ notes that the posts do not say whether the CNCF has accepted it, and that Docker Sandboxes is so far the only product that supports it, so working across different products has not been shown.
notes: Read the full InfoQ article from the fulltext file. Event of 24 Sep 2026 is before 2 Oct 2026, so it may be held back as older news. v1_category kept as default MOD.
